body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فيقول المؤلف رحمه الله: باب مخارج الحروف الباب في اللغة فرجة في ساتر يتوصل بها من داخل إلى خارج وبالعكس حقيقةً في المباني كباب الدار وحكما في المعاني كباب مخارج الحروف، وهو في الاصطلاح اسم لطائفة من الفن تشترك في بعض الأحكام وتتميز عن غيرها، وهو يعقد لما يحتاج لبيانه من العلم، فهذا العلم الذي هو علم الأداء من مسائله التي تحتاج إلى عقد باب مخارج الحروف، والحروف قد سبق تعريفها وهي يبٍحث فيها من أربعة أوجه، الوجه الأول: المخرج (مخرج الحرف)، والوجه الثاني الصفة التي يتصف بها الحرف، والوجه الثالث الشكل أي الضبط الذي يكون عليه سكونا أو حركة، والوجه الرابع العوارض الصوتية عند التركيب كالإدغام والترقيق وغير ذلك من العوارض الصوتية، فمن أتقن هذه الأمور الأربعة كلٌّ على حدة استطاع أداء الحرف على وجهه الصحيح، ومن عرف بعضها دون بعض لا بد أن يدخل عليه الخلل والخطأ من جهة ما جهل منها..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the author says, may God have mercy on him: "Chapter on the points of articulation of the letters." Bāb in the language is an opening in a barrier by which one passes from inside to outside and the reverse — literally so in buildings, as with the door of a house, and by attribution in matters of meaning, as with the "chapter" on the points of articulation of the letters. As a technical term it is a name for a group of topics within a discipline which share certain rulings and are distinguished from others; it is set out for whatever in the science needs explaining. This science, which is the science of performance (ʿilm al-adāʾ), has among its topics those that require a chapter on the points of articulation of the letters to be set out. The letters have already been defined. They are investigated from four aspects. The first aspect: the point of articulation (the makhraj of the letter). The second aspect: the quality by which the letter is characterised. The third aspect: the form, that is, the marking it bears, whether quiescence or a vowel. The fourth aspect: the phonetic accidents that arise on combination, such as assimilation (idghām) and thinning (tarqīq) and other phonetic accidents. Whoever masters these four matters, each one separately, is able to perform the letter in its correct form; and whoever knows some of them and not others will inevitably fall into flaw and error from the side of what he did not know of them..

flags.context: فهذا العلم الذي هو علم الأداء
flags.note: HOMONYM WITH A GLOSSARY ENTRY. The glossary fixes adāʾ as 'performance in its proper time', its sense in the law of worship, where it is opposed to qaḍāʾ, making up a missed act. That sense has nothing to do with this passage: ʿilm al-adāʾ is the science of how the Qur'an is correctly uttered, a synonym in this literature for tajwīd. Applying the glossary entry here would make the sentence unintelligible. The same trap as at id 629 with ʿilal and at id 636 with muṭlaq; the glossary needs a note on each of these three.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on the Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, Ibn al-Jazari's versified primer on the rules of Qur'anic recitation. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 641–646 and the part numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the number in the title, not by id.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Points of articulation' renders makhārij, the places in the mouth and throat at which each letter is produced.
'Quiescence or a vowel' renders sukūnan aw ḥarakatan — whether the letter carries no vowel or carries one.

'Phonetic accidents' renders al-ʿawāriḍ al-ṣawtiyyah, changes that come upon a letter only when it is combined with others; idghām is the assimilation of one letter into the next, tarqīq the thinning or lightening of a sound as against its being pronounced heavy.
The source prints يبٍحث with a stray kasratan over the bāʾ, a typographical artefact with no bearing on the sense. It is preserved in body_ar.

The definition of bāb ('chapter', literally 'door') as an opening in a barrier is a piece of lexical play the Sheikh is making deliberately, and has been kept rather than replaced by the bare word 'chapter'.
